question: If the slope of a distance-time graph changes continuously, it indicates:
solution:
The correct answer is __**non-uniform speed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In a **distance-time graph**, the **slope** of the line represents the **speed** of the object. The mathematical relationship is defined as **Speed = Distance / Time**.
 
• If the **slope changes continuously**, it indicates that the **speed** of the object is not constant over time. This variation in speed is referred to as **non-uniform speed**. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• A **curved line** on a distance-time graph is the visual representation of **non-uniform motion**. The curvature indicates that the object is either **speeding up (accelerating)** or **slowing down (decelerating)**.
 
• For **non-uniform speed**, the object covers **unequal distances** in **equal intervals of time**. For example, a car moving through heavy traffic frequently changes its speed, resulting in a non-linear graph.<
